subject: Data erasure window & backup snapshot policy — post-demo questions
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@healthbridge.com>, John Patel <john.patel@healthbridge.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 14:12:00 -0400
Subject: Data erasure window & backup snapshot policy — post-demo questions

Hi Claire / John,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — appreciated the concrete examples you shared around data retention and audit windows. I promised a short recap + 3 specific questions so you have something to share with your legal/compliance team.

Recap (high level):
- Redwood serves inference and stores model request metadata and application logs required for debugging and analytics.
- We keep primary operational logs and application data in region-specific object storage; backups and point-in-time snapshots are retained in a separate long-term snapshot store.
- We support account-level retention configuration and produce audit logs for delete requests.

Questions / asks:
1) Deletion SLA scope: For deletion requests from HealthBridge, do you require purging from "primary + backups/snapshots" within a single calendar window (e.g., 30 days), or is a two-stage approach acceptable (logical deletion immediately; physical purge on next backup rotation)?
2) Snapshot retention expectations: What is your maximum acceptable snapshot TTL? We mentioned default snapshot retention is 180 days; is that acceptable or do you need shorter (e.g., 90 days) or longer?
3) Evidence & attestation: Please confirm which artifacts you need from us to close your questionnaire items (SOC 2 status, proof of deletion flows, backup retention docs). Attached is our redwood-data-retention-playbook.pdf — see section 3 (Backup & Snapshot Handling) for the current canonical wording.

Next steps I propose:
- If you confirm target TTL and deletion window, I will route this to Product + Security to propose exact SLA wording and an optional expedited-erasure offering for contracts.
- If you prefer, we can open a vendor security questionnaire (VSA) and I can return a populated copy within 48 hours.

Callout: We are SOC 2 Type II in progress (control run started Jun 2027); I will share an ETA in the next note.

Attachments: redwood-data-retention-playbook.pdf (section 3), s3-snapshot-policy.docx

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-min follow-up if helpful.

Best,
Diego

From: Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@healthbridge.com>

Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data erasure window & backup snapshot policy — post-demo questions

Thanks Diego — useful summary. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- For our regulated datasets (PHI), legal requires deletion to be "completed" (including backups) within 30 days of a formal delete request. We understand snapshots complicate that, but 30 days is their expectation unless we can provide a technical compensating control (e.g., cryptographic key destruction) that would be considered equivalent.
- For non-PHI telemetry, we can accept a longer snapshot TTL (90–180 days).
- For evidence: our InfoSec team will want (a) a statement of your SOC 2 status and target date, (b) a short description of the deletion flow with timestamps, and (c) a filled VSA. I've attached our VSA_questionnaire.xlsx; if you can pre-fill sections A1–A5 that would be great.

Would you be able to confirm whether Redwood supports: 
1) cryptographic erasure for backups (via customer-managed keys) such that we can meet the 30-day requirement for PHI?
2) an enterprise add-on for expedited purges (if cryptographic erasure isn't available)?

Happy to take a short call with product/security if that expedites things.

Best,
Claire

Diego / team — thanks for the ping. Quick summary of what we can offer and proposed wording for the VSA / MSA.

1) Current default behavior (no BYOK):
- Logical deletion: immediate (within minutes) after formal request; data becomes inaccessible for normal read operations.
- Physical removal from backups/snapshots: occurs on normal backup rotation. Typical rotation for our snapshot store is 45–60 days, so physical purge can be expected within that window. We do not guarantee immediate physical purge without an expedited contract.

2) BYOK / KMS-backed crypto erasure:
- If the customer uses customer-managed keys (BYOK) and requests key destruction, we can provide cryptographic erasure for backups much faster. Wording to propose for VSA: "When customer uses customer-managed encryption keys, Redwood performs cryptographic erasure by decommissioning or rotating keys upon verified deletion request, rendering snapshots and backups unreadable. Customers are responsible for the lifecycle of their keys and confirmation of destruction as applicable."

3) Expedited purge offering (enterprise add-on):
- We can offer an expedited-purge service (one-time fee / annual retainer) that triggers accelerated ingestion of snapshot removals and prioritizes physical purge processes; SLA target: 14–30 days depending on snapshot size and region. Exact lead time will be scoped during SOW.

4) Evidence & SOC 2:
- SOC 2 Type II: Control run in progress; expected report availability ~2028-02-01. We can provide interim attestation of controls and sample deletion logs on request under NDA.

Proposed language for HealthBridge VSA / MSA: 
- "Redwood performs logical deletion immediately upon customer request. Physical removal from backups and snapshots occurs on backup rotation; typical window is 45–60 days. For customers using customer-managed keys, cryptographic erasure is available upon key destruction (subject to key lifecycle controls). Redwood also offers an expedited-purge add-on with a contractual SLA of 14–30 days for physical removal, to be scoped in the SOW"

I'll also attach a short excerpt for the MSA and ask security to confirm the exact SOC timeline and what artifacts we can share over NDA. Let me know if you want me to populate the VSA_Questionnaire.xlsx and return to Claire.

—Ben
